Workflow Guide

A quick-start guide to the SKEBA AI workflow: starting-image context, audio denoise, Live Playlist registration, the Reference Library, LLM prompt skills, and the recommended prompt structure.

Follow SKEBA AI on PatreonLLM Prompt Skill

Quick Start

1. Configure workflow→2. Add references→3. Write tagged prompt→4. Generate→5. Use Live Playlist

Core Workflow Controls

1

Starting Image

Starts the prompt sequence using an image as visual context. Set Starting Image? to true when you want the generation to begin from the supplied image.

2

Audio Denoise

Adds an extra 4-step audio processing pass to improve output quality. This is especially useful when generating with Turbo LoRAs.

3

Register / Update Playlist Workflow

Click this control and assign a name to register or update the current workflow. This links the workflow to the Live Playlist.

4

Open Reference Library

Opens the Reference Library used to manage reusable characters, locations, objects, images, audio, video, and experimental reference modifications.

Reference Library

The Reference Library lets prompts use semantic tags such as {Character_Name} and voice references such as §Character_Name§. Matching reference material is injected automatically by the workflow.

FeatureWhat it doesTypical use
ReferencesStores images, sound, and video and automatically injects matching references when their tags are used.Characters, locations, objects, voices, source video, and other reusable assets.
Built-in CharactersCharacters known to work as built-in model knowledge.Use a built-in character directly, then optionally add images or sound for stronger visual or voice guidance.
Additional ReferencesAdds extra image and audio material to a character or asset.Further fine-tuning of appearance, wardrobe, voice, or other characteristics.
RefModsExperimental system that trains from video, images, and audio so an identity or concept can be injected without consuming a normal reference.Experimental reusable character/style injection when reference slots are limited or a trained representation is preferred.
Tip: Keep tag names consistent. A saved visual reference uses curly braces, for example {Jerry Seinfeld_BC}, while its saved voice is referenced inside dialogue with section signs, for example §Jerry Seinfeld_BC§.

LLM Prompt Skill

For an LLM-ready set of rules for generating prompts compatible with the workflow, use the SKEBA MiniMax prompt skill:

SKEBA MiniMax Skill — GitHub

General Prompt Format

The workflow uses a compact tagged structure. A typical prompt contains a control line followed by four main sections.

PartPurpose
[new_location]Marks the beginning of a new physical location instead of continuing the previous clip's visual context.
[s=15]Sets the requested clip duration/control value used by the workflow.
subject_definitionsDefines referenced characters, wardrobe continuity, locations, objects, and other important subject-level constraints.
detailed_descriptionDefines the overall visual treatment, scene, blocking, style, pacing, and the shot-by-shot timeline.
overall_soundscapeDefines environmental audio, sound effects, room tone, audience reactions, and other diegetic sound.
non_diegetic_musicDefines score or music that exists outside the physical scene. Use N/A when none is needed.

Minimal Example

This deliberately short example demonstrates the syntax without the extra detail of a production prompt.

[new_location] [s=15]

subject_definitions:

{Jerry Seinfeld_BC} Wardrobe: wearing a dark navy button-up shirt, blue jeans, and white athletic sneakers. This exact wardrobe remains fixed throughout the clip.

{George Costanza_BC} Wardrobe: wearing a muted olive-green button-up shirt, tan trousers, and dark brown shoes. This exact wardrobe remains fixed throughout the clip.

{Monks_Coffee}

detailed_description:

Live-action early-1990s multi-camera sitcom scene inside {Monks_Coffee}, with warm diner lighting, natural sitcom blocking, energetic pacing, and a responsive studio audience laugh track.

timeline:

[Shot 1] At 00:00, a medium-wide establishing shot shows {Jerry Seinfeld_BC} and {George Costanza_BC} seated in their booth.

[Shot 2] At 00:03, camera cuts to only {Jerry Seinfeld_BC}. Jerry says, <d>[English §Jerry Seinfeld_BC§]I'm talking about lesbians!</d>

A quick audience laugh follows.

[Shot 3] At 00:07, camera cuts to only {George Costanza_BC}. George reacts silently while staring at Jerry.

overall_soundscape:

Subdued coffee-shop ambience, plates and silverware, cups touching saucers, and a responsive studio audience laugh track.

non_diegetic_music:

N/A

Dialogue Syntax

Dialogue is wrapped in <d>...</d>. Put the language and saved voice reference inside square brackets, followed immediately by the spoken words.

<d>[English §Jerry Seinfeld_BC§]Spoken dialogue goes here.</d>

The character's visual tag and voice tag can share the same saved name, but they use different delimiters: { } for the visual reference and § § for the voice reference.

Recommended Authoring Pattern

Define continuity first

Lock important wardrobe and character details in subject_definitions so they remain explicit throughout the generation.

Describe the production style

At the beginning of detailed_description, establish whether the scene is cinematic, sitcom, documentary, horror, animation, or another visual language.

Use timed shots

Break the action into [Shot 1], [Shot 2], and so on. Add timestamps when timing matters.

Bind every voice explicitly

For spoken dialogue, keep the voice reference inside the language brackets so the intended speaker and voice remain tightly associated.

Presented by SKEBA AI · Workflow documentation quick guide · Patreon · GitHub Repository
